writes.rule: Per subtopic seen: pMastery 0.7 if right at D2/D3, 0.55 if right at D1, 0.25 if wrong; level L0-L3 from the ladder step reached
Prerequisite-gap index = 100 x weighted misses / weighted items seen in slots 1-4, averaged over groups
Groups with the highest Part A percent (top 1-2, only if >= 65%)
Groups with the lowest Part A percent (bottom 1-2, only if < 65%)
Calibration = 1 - mean |confidence/5 - correct| over Part A (feeds the first MCI reading)
Highest difficulty answered correctly twice in a row: D1 low, D2 medium, D3 high
Verbal reasoning = percent of Part B verbal items right
Numerical reasoning = percent of Part B numerical items right
Abstract reasoning = percent of Part B abstract items right
Spatial reasoning = percent of Part B spatial items right
Logical deduction = percent right on Part B items tagged p65
Numeracy fluency = numerical percent scaled by speed (right answers under target time count 1.2x, max 100)
Processing speed = 100 x share of Part B items answered right within target seconds
RIASEC profile: each career-interest item scored 1-5; letter score = mean of its 2 items; top 3 letters form the code (e.g. IRC)

items.stem: Factorise x² + 5x + 6.
items.markingKey: C. (x + 2)(x + 3). Find two numbers that multiply to 6 and add to 5

items.stem: What is the gradient of the line y = 3x - 2?
items.subtopicHint: Gradient and intercept of a straight line
items.markingKey: C. 3. In y = mx + c, m is the gradient

items.stem: What is the gradient of the line through (1, 2) and (4, 11)?
items.subtopicHint: Gradient and intercept of a straight line

items.stem: A bag holds 3 red and 5 blue counters. One is picked at random. What is the probability it is red?
items.subtopicHint: Probability of equally likely and combined outcomes
items.markingKey: B. 3/8. 3 red out of 8 counters

items.stem: A fair die is rolled. What is the probability of getting a number greater than 4?
items.subtopicHint: Probability of equally likely and combined outcomes
items.markingKey: A. 1/3. Only 5 and 6 work: 2 out of 6

items.stem: Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting at least one head?
items.subtopicHint: Probability of equally likely and combined outcomes
items.markingKey: B. 3/4. HH, HT, TH out of HH, HT, TH, TT

items.stem: What is the mean of 4, 7, 9, 12 and 8?
What is the median of 3, 9, 4, 7, 12 and 5?
items.markingKey: B. 6. Order: 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12; middle pair (5 + 7) ÷ 2

items.stem: The mean of five numbers is 12. One number, 20, is removed. What is the mean of the other four?
What is the HCF of 12 and 18?
items.subtopicHint: HCF and LCM by prime factorisation
items.markingKey: C. 6. 12 = 2² x 3 and 18 = 2 x 3², so HCF = 2 x 3

items.stem: The HCF of two numbers is 6 and their LCM is 72. One number is 18. What is the other?
items.subtopicHint: HCF and LCM by prime factorisation
items.markingKey: C. 24. HCF x LCM = product, so 6 x 72 ÷ 18 = 24

items.stem: Two bells ring every 12 and 20 minutes. They ring together at 9:00. When do they next ring together?
items.subtopicHint: HCF and LCM by prime factorisation

items.stem: Which of these numbers is irrational?
items.markingKey: C. √3. 3 is not a perfect square

items.stem: If √2 is irrational, which of these must also be irrational?
items.markingKey: D. 5 + √2. Rational + irrational is irrational; the others equal 0, 2 and 4

items.stem: To prove √5 is irrational, we assume √5 = a/b in lowest terms. Which step follows?
options: a and b must both be even
items.markingKey: A. 5b² = a², so 5 divides a. Squaring gives a² = 5b², leading to a contradiction

items.stem: What are the zeroes of x² - 5x + 6?
items.subtopicHint: Zeroes and coefficients of a quadratic polynomial

items.stem: For x² - 7x + 10, what is the sum of the zeroes?
items.subtopicHint: Zeroes and coefficients of a quadratic polynomial
items.markingKey: C. 7. Sum = -b/a = 7

items.stem: Which quadratic polynomial has zeroes whose sum is 4 and product is -5?
items.subtopicHint: Zeroes and coefficients of a quadratic polynomial
items.markingKey: D. x² - 4x - 5. x² - (sum)x + product

items.stem: Solve x + y = 10 and x - y = 2.
items.subtopicHint: Solving a pair of linear equations by elimination
items.markingKey: C. x = 6, y = 4. Adding gives 2x = 12

items.stem: Solve 2x + 3y = 13 and x + 3y = 8.
items.subtopicHint: Solving a pair of linear equations by elimination
items.markingKey: B. x = 5, y = 1. Subtracting gives x = 5

items.stem: Two pens and three notebooks cost 110. Four pens and one notebook cost 70. What does one notebook cost?
items.subtopicHint: Solving a pair of linear equations by elimination
items.markingKey: B. 30. Double the first: 4p + 6n = 220; subtract to get 5n = 150

items.stem: A 1200 kg car accelerates at 2 m/s². What resultant force acts on it?
Sodium has the electron arrangement 2,8,1. How many electrons are in its outer shell?
items.markingKey: B. 1. The last number is the outer shell

items.stem: An element has the electron arrangement 2,8,7. What happens when it forms an ion?
items.answer: It gains one electron to form a 1- ion
options: It loses seven electrons to form a 7+ ion
It loses one electron to form a 1+ ion
It gains one electron to form a 1- ion
items.markingKey: C. It gains one electron to form a 1- ion. Gaining one electron completes the outer shell (chlorine)

items.stem: Magnesium forms Mg²⁺ ions and oxygen forms O²⁻ ions. What is the formula of magnesium oxide?
items.markingKey: A. MgO. The charges balance one to one

items.stem: Aluminium forms Al³⁺ ions and oxygen forms O²⁻ ions. What is the formula of aluminium oxide?
items.markingKey: C. Al₂O₃. 2 x (+3) balances 3 x (-2)

items.stem: Which equation is correctly balanced?
items.markingKey: A. 4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃. Count atoms: 4 Fe and 6 O on each side

items.stem: A cyclist speeds up from 0 to 20 m/s in 5 s. What is the acceleration?
items.markingKey: D. 4 m/s². a = change in velocity ÷ time

items.stem: On a velocity-time graph, what does the area under the line show?
items.markingKey: B. The distance travelled. Area = velocity x time

items.stem: A car moving at 20 m/s brakes steadily to rest in 4 s. How far does it travel while braking?
items.markingKey: B. 40 m. Area of the triangle: ½ x 4 x 20

items.stem: In a chemical equation, the substances on the left of the arrow are the
items.markingKey: C. reactants. Reactants change into products

items.stem: Balance: Mg + O₂ → MgO
items.markingKey: B. 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO. Two O atoms on the left need two MgO on the right

items.stem: What does the symbol (aq) mean in NaCl(aq)?
items.markingKey: C. Dissolved in water. Aqueous means in water solution

items.stem: CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ is a
items.markingKey: B. combination reaction. Two substances join to make one

items.stem: An iron nail placed in copper sulfate solution turns brown and the blue colour fades. What type of reaction is this?
items.markingKey: D. Displacement. Iron is more reactive and displaces copper

items.stem: Silver chloride turns grey in sunlight. Which type of reaction is this?
items.markingKey: B. Photolytic decomposition. Light breaks AgCl into silver and chlorine

items.stem: A solution with pH 2 is
items.markingKey: A. strongly acidic. pH below 7 is acidic

items.stem: Why does an antacid relieve acidity in the stomach?
items.answer: It is a mild base that neutralises excess acid
options: It is a mild base that neutralises excess acid
It is an acid that adds to the stomach acid
items.markingKey: B. It is a mild base that neutralises excess acid. Bases neutralise acids

items.stem: Tooth decay starts when the pH in the mouth falls below about 5.5. Why does this happen after eating sugary food?
items.answer: Bacteria break down sugar and produce acids
options: Bacteria break down sugar and produce acids
items.markingKey: D. Bacteria break down sugar and produce acids. Acid attacks the enamel

items.stem: Which metal reacts most vigorously with cold water?
items.markingKey: B. potassium. Potassium is at the top of the series

items.stem: Why is gold used in jewellery?
items.answer: It is very unreactive and does not tarnish
options: It is very unreactive and does not tarnish
items.markingKey: C. It is very unreactive and does not tarnish. Gold is at the bottom of the series

items.stem: Zinc is added to copper sulfate solution and copper is added to zinc sulfate solution. What happens?
items.markingKey: A. Only the first mixture reacts. Zinc is more reactive than copper and displaces it

items.stem: Read: "Meera glanced at the clock again, tapped her pen and read the same line for the fifth time." How is Meera most likely feeling?
items.markingKey: D. Restless and unable to concentrate. Repeated glancing and rereading suggest restlessness

items.stem: In 'The wind howled through the empty streets', the wind is given a human or animal quality. This is
items.markingKey: A. personification. An object is given living qualities

items.stem: What is the effect of 'the classroom was a pressure cooker before the exam'?
items.answer: It shows the tension was building and about to burst
options: It shows the students were hungry
It shows the tension was building and about to burst
It shows the classroom was hot from cooking
It shows the exam was easy
items.markingKey: B. It shows the tension was building and about to burst. A pressure cooker builds pressure until it releases

items.stem: In an argument, the main point the writer wants you to accept is the
items.markingKey: C. claim. Evidence supports the claim

items.stem: Which sentence is a counterargument in an essay arguing for school uniforms?
items.answer: Some say uniforms limit students' self-expression.
options: Uniforms reduce peer pressure about clothes.
A 2023 survey found most parents support uniforms.
Some say uniforms limit students' self-expression.
items.markingKey: D. Some say uniforms limit students' self-expression.. A counterargument presents the opposing view

items.stem: A writer says: 'Everyone I know hates homework, so homework should be banned.' What is the main weakness?
items.answer: The evidence is a small, personal sample
options: It is written in the first person
The evidence is a small, personal sample
items.markingKey: D. The evidence is a small, personal sample. A few friends do not represent everyone

items.stem: Which of these is a complex sentence?
items.answer: When the bell rang, the students rushed out.
options: When the bell rang, the students rushed out.
The bell rang and the students rushed out.
items.markingKey: B. When the bell rang, the students rushed out.. It has a main clause and a subordinate clause

items.stem: A story reads: 'The door creaked. Silence. Then footsteps.' What is the effect of the short sentences?
options: They make the story feel relaxed
They show the writer ran out of ideas
They explain the setting in detail
items.markingKey: D. They build tension and suspense. Short, broken sentences slow the reader and create suspense

items.stem: Rearrange into a correct sentence: "the / finally / after / rain / match / the / began / the / stopped"
items.answer: The match finally began after the rain stopped.
options: The match stopped after the rain finally began.
The rain finally began after the match stopped.
The match finally began after the rain stopped.
After the match finally began the rain stopped.
items.markingKey: C. The match finally began after the rain stopped.. The match could only start once the rain had stopped

items.stem: Why did Lencho write a letter to God?
items.answer: A hailstorm had destroyed his crop and he needed money
items.subtopicHint: A Letter to God: faith and irony
options: He wanted to complain about the postmaster
He wished to sell his land
He wanted to thank God for rain
A hailstorm had destroyed his crop and he needed money
items.markingKey: D. A hailstorm had destroyed his crop and he needed money. He had faith that God would help

items.stem: Why did the postmaster send Lencho money?
items.answer: He did not want to shake Lencho's faith in God
items.subtopicHint: A Letter to God: faith and irony
options: He did not want to shake Lencho's faith in God
He wanted to keep the letter
items.markingKey: A. He did not want to shake Lencho's faith in God. He was moved by Lencho's faith

items.stem: What is ironic about the end of the story?
items.answer: Lencho thanks God but calls the post office employees crooks
items.subtopicHint: A Letter to God: faith and irony
options: Lencho thanks God but calls the post office employees crooks
The postmaster asks Lencho for money
items.markingKey: A. Lencho thanks God but calls the post office employees crooks. He suspects the very people who helped him

items.stem: Choose the correct form: Lencho ___ the field every morning.
items.markingKey: C. checks. Simple present with a singular subject

items.stem: Choose the correct form: By the time the rain stopped, the hail ___ the crop.
items.markingKey: B. had destroyed. Past perfect for the earlier of two past actions

items.stem: Find the error: "He said that he will write to God the next day."
items.markingKey: A. 'will' should be 'would'. Reported past needs would

items.stem: In Dust of Snow, what falls on the poet?
items.answer: dust of snow from a hemlock tree
items.subtopicHint: Dust of Snow: symbolism and change of mood
options: dust of snow from a hemlock tree
items.markingKey: D. dust of snow from a hemlock tree. A crow shakes it down

items.stem: The crow and the hemlock usually suggest
items.subtopicHint: Dust of Snow: symbolism and change of mood
items.markingKey: A. gloom and sorrow. Frost uses unusual symbols of sadness

items.stem: What is the poem's central message?
items.answer: A small moment of nature can change a bad mood
items.subtopicHint: Dust of Snow: symbolism and change of mood
options: A small moment of nature can change a bad mood
items.markingKey: C. A small moment of nature can change a bad mood. The day is 'saved' from regret

items.stem: In 'Fire and Ice', fire stands for
items.subtopicHint: Fire and Ice: symbolism and understatement
items.markingKey: B. desire. Fire is linked to desire

items.stem: What does ice symbolise in the poem?
items.subtopicHint: Fire and Ice: symbolism and understatement
items.markingKey: A. hatred. Ice stands for cold, indifferent hatred

items.stem: When Frost says ice 'would suffice' to destroy the world, the line is an example of
items.subtopicHint: Fire and Ice: symbolism and understatement
items.markingKey: D. understatement. Destruction of the world is described in a calm, mild word

items.stem: In a democracy, the final decision-making power rests with
items.markingKey: B. representatives elected by the people. Rule by the people through elected representatives

items.stem: Who conducts elections to the Lok Sabha in India?
items.subtopicHint: Election Commission and free and fair elections
items.markingKey: C. the Election Commission. An independent constitutional body

items.stem: Why is the Model Code of Conduct important during elections?
items.answer: It sets rules so that parties and candidates compete fairly
items.subtopicHint: Election Commission and free and fair elections
options: It sets rules so that parties and candidates compete fairly
It bans voting by young people
It lets the ruling party campaign longer
items.markingKey: B. It sets rules so that parties and candidates compete fairly. It prevents misuse of power during campaigns

items.stem: When the price of a good rises, other things staying the same, the quantity demanded usually
items.subtopicHint: Demand: how buyers respond to price
items.markingKey: C. falls. The law of demand

items.stem: Which of these would increase the demand for umbrellas?
items.subtopicHint: Demand: how buyers respond to price
items.markingKey: A. The start of the monsoon. A change in need shifts demand

items.stem: Petrol prices rise sharply. What is likely to happen to the demand for electric scooters?
items.answer: It rises, because they are a substitute
items.subtopicHint: Demand: how buyers respond to price
options: It falls, because they are a complement
It rises, because they are a substitute
items.markingKey: C. It rises, because they are a substitute. Buyers switch to substitutes

items.stem: The price at which the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied is the
items.markingKey: C. market (equilibrium) price. Demand and supply meet

items.stem: If the price is above the equilibrium, there will be a
items.markingKey: C. surplus. Sellers offer more than buyers want

items.stem: A bad harvest cuts the supply of onions. What happens to the market price and quantity sold?
items.markingKey: B. Price rises and quantity falls. Supply shifts left

items.stem: Who led the unification of Germany?
items.markingKey: A. Otto von Bismarck. The Prussian chief minister

items.stem: Garibaldi's Red Shirts helped unify Italy by
items.answer: conquering the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies in the south
options: conquering the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies in the south
items.markingKey: A. conquering the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies in the south. They marched through southern Italy in 1860

items.stem: Bismarck's policy of 'blood and iron' meant that Germany was unified mainly through
options: a liberal revolution of the people
items.markingKey: C. wars led by Prussia. Wars with Denmark, Austria and France

items.stem: Gandhiji's method of mass agitation based on truth and non-violence is called
items.subtopicHint: Rowlatt Act, Jallianwala Bagh and satyagraha
items.markingKey: C. satyagraha. The power of truth

items.stem: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 was opposed because it
items.answer: allowed political prisoners to be detained without trial
items.subtopicHint: Rowlatt Act, Jallianwala Bagh and satyagraha
options: allowed political prisoners to be detained without trial
items.markingKey: B. allowed political prisoners to be detained without trial. It gave the government sweeping powers

items.stem: Why did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre turn many moderates against British rule?
items.answer: It showed the government would use brutal force against peaceful crowds
items.subtopicHint: Rowlatt Act, Jallianwala Bagh and satyagraha
options: It ended the First World War
It led to the Salt March the next day
It showed the government would use brutal force against peaceful crowds
It was ordered by Indian leaders
items.markingKey: C. It showed the government would use brutal force against peaceful crowds. General Dyer fired on an unarmed gathering

items.stem: The Salt March of 1930 ended at
items.subtopicHint: Civil Disobedience and the Salt March
items.markingKey: A. Dandi. Gandhiji walked from Sabarmati to Dandi

items.stem: Why did Gandhiji choose salt as the symbol of protest?
items.answer: Salt was used by rich and poor alike, so the tax hurt everyone
items.subtopicHint: Civil Disobedience and the Salt March
options: Salt was made only in Britain
Salt was used by rich and poor alike, so the tax hurt everyone
Salt was only used by the British
items.markingKey: B. Salt was used by rich and poor alike, so the tax hurt everyone. It united all sections of society

items.stem: How did the Civil Disobedience Movement differ from Non-Cooperation?
items.answer: People were asked to break colonial laws, not just refuse to cooperate
items.subtopicHint: Civil Disobedience and the Salt March
options: People were asked to break colonial laws, not just refuse to cooperate
items.markingKey: B. People were asked to break colonial laws, not just refuse to cooperate. Breaking the salt law was a direct challenge

items.stem: The Great Depression began around
items.markingKey: B. 1929. With the Wall Street crash

items.stem: How did the Great Depression affect Indian farmers?
items.answer: Crop prices fell sharply but land revenue demands stayed high
options: Crop prices fell sharply but land revenue demands stayed high
items.markingKey: C. Crop prices fell sharply but land revenue demands stayed high. Peasants fell into debt

items.stem: Why did the Depression help build support for the Civil Disobedience Movement in the countryside?
items.answer: Distressed peasants were angry about high revenue at a time of low prices
options: Factories in India closed for good
Distressed peasants were angry about high revenue at a time of low prices
Farmers became richer and wanted more
items.markingKey: B. Distressed peasants were angry about high revenue at a time of low prices. Economic hardship fed political protest

items.stem: What number comes next? 5, 10, 20, 40, ?

items.explanation: Snakes are inside the reptile group, which has no fur; the last option may be true but does not follow

items.stem: Five friends sit in a row. P is at one end and Q sits next to P. R is in the middle seat. S does not sit next to R. Where does T sit?
items.explanation: Seats 1-5: P, Q, R; S cannot be in 4, so S is in 5 and T in 4

items.stem: Which letter comes next? Z, X, V, T, ?
items.explanation: Go back two letters each time

items.stem: In a code, CAT is written DBU. How is DOG written?
items.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward

items.stem: An arrow turns 90° clockwise at each step. Step 1 points up, step 2 right, step 3 down. Which way does it point at step 6?
items.explanation: The cycle repeats every 4 steps; step 6 = step 2

items.stem: In a 3 x 3 grid every row and column has one circle, one square and one triangle. Row 1: circle, square, triangle. Row 2: triangle, circle, square. What goes in row 3, column 2?
items.explanation: Column 2 already has a square and a circle
